project_structure.description: An agentic "software factory" template repository (ADR-002). It is not an application codebase with a src/ tree; instead it is primarily composed of AI-agent Skills (.devin/skills/), Rules, Hooks, a vault/ knowledge base, and a promptfoo-based eval harness (evals/) that grades skill outputs. There is currently no implementation code for the Cadence Story Analysis Workflow itself (no workflow/, worker/, or activity source files exist anywhere in the repo) — only reference documentation and example snippets provided by the `cadence-workflow-orchestration` skill. The story under analysis asks for that Cadence implementation to be built for the first time.

unit_testing_tools: promptfoo eval (YAML-driven skill/prompt evals in evals/)
bash + jq assertions in each skill's verify.sh

subprojects.description: SDLC skill library. Each skill is a self-contained folder with a SKILL.md (instructions), schema/ (JSON Schemas + examples for its output), and a verify.sh (bash+jq quantitative verification script) per ADR-003/ADR-004. Skills relevant to this story: extract-story-intent, analyze-story, grade-story-analysis, repair-story-analysis (all already implemented), plus the new reference skill cadence-workflow-orchestration which documents how to build Cadence workflows/activities/workers in Go and Python but contains no runnable project code beyond isolated examples/ snippets (hello_world_workflow.py, worker_setup.py).

Reference-only documentation skill for Cadence (workflows, activities, workers, task lists, Go and Python client SDKs, CLI/HTTP API, debugging playbooks) plus minimal illustrative examples/go and examples/python snippets (hello-world workflow + worker setup). No actual Story Analysis Workflow, Activities, or Worker exist here or anywhere else in the repo — this is the knowledge source the new implementation must be built from, not existing implementation to reuse directly.

tech_stack.programming_language: Python / Go (examples only, not wired into any app)

subprojects.description: Hook scripts invoked by .devin/hooks.json (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/SessionEnd) that verify secrets, run skill verify.sh on sentinel-file completion (ADR-004), and log conversation/audit data. lib/common.sh provides shared bash helpers (stdin JSON parsing, changed-file detection, logging).

promptfoo-based eval suites (YAML) that grade each skill's LLM output (extractStoryIntent, gradeAnalysis, gradeDesign, designImplementation) against expected structure/quality; run via `npm test` (promptfoo eval).

decisions.why: Establishes that this repo is skills-based and that Workflows coordinate skill invocation — directly informs how the Cadence Workflow should sequence extract-story-intent -> analyze-story -> grade-story-analysis -> repair-story-analysis as Activities wrapping existing skills.

Defines the sentinel-file (.process/{skill}.done.json) and verify.sh contract each skill Activity must still honor when invoked from inside a Cadence Activity, and how a verification hook currently detects skill completion outside of any workflow engine.
Describes the quantitative (verify.sh) vs. qualitative (grader skill) split used by grade-story-analysis, which the Workflow's grade/repair loop must preserve when invoking that Activity.

Defines the grade-story-analysis rubric/pass-threshold pattern (fixed floor, e.g. 80%) that the Workflow's bounded 3-attempt grade-repair loop must check against to decide whether to invoke repair-story-analysis again or escalate.

Skills read their input documents directly rather than relying on a fixed upstream schema; the Cadence Activities wrapping each skill should pass file paths/content rather than tightly-coupled in-memory objects, preserving this loose coupling across Activity boundaries.

Confirms this repo's documentation must remain usable by both humans and agents — relevant to the story's acceptance criterion that the new Workflow/Activity/Worker code be documented well enough for another engineer to run it unaided.

target_architecture.why: Index/reference architecture for how Workflows, Activities, Workers, Task Lists, and the Cadence service fit together; the story's target architecture (Python client SDK, local embedded-SQLite server, Worker polling a Task List, Signal-based human escalation) is defined here, not yet implemented as project code.
Documents the Python client SDK patterns (workflow/activity decorators, invoking activities from a workflow) that the new Story Analysis Workflow implementation must follow.
Documents RetryPolicy configuration and ActivityFailure handling needed to satisfy the story's retry and error-handling acceptance criteria.
Documents Signal/Query handling needed for the human-escalation acceptance criteria (ambiguous step, exhausted grade-repair loop, escalation timeout).
Documents running a local Cadence server (embedded SQLite) and first workflow, which the story's infrastructure dependencies (local domain registration, task list) rely on.

services.why: Existing SDLC skill (SKILL.md + schema/story-intent.schema.json + verify.sh) to be wrapped as the Workflow's first Cadence Activity; already writes a sentinel file per ADR-004 that the Activity wrapper can reuse or emulate.
Existing SDLC skill to be wrapped as the Workflow's second Cadence Activity (analyze-story), producing the analysis.json consumed by grade-story-analysis.

Existing grader skill (ADR-006 pattern: rubric.md, fixed pass-threshold, analysis-grade.schema.json) to be wrapped as the Cadence Activity that decides whether the grade-repair loop continues or the Workflow proceeds/escalates.

Already-implemented skill (SKILL.md, schema/analysis.schema.json, verify.sh) that repairs an analysis using grader feedback; to be wrapped as the Cadence Activity invoked on each repair attempt, bounded to 3 attempts by the Workflow.
Only existing runnable Cadence Python example in the repo; a minimal single-activity workflow that is the closest existing pattern to model the new multi-Activity, looping Story Analysis Workflow on.

Only existing example of registering a Worker against a domain/task list with the Python client; pattern to reuse for the new Worker process that will host the Story Analysis Workflow and its four Activities.
Shared bash helpers used by hooks/skills for sentinel/log handling; relevant if the new repository-state-affecting Activities need to follow the same logging/sentinel conventions as existing skills.

models.why: Defines the shape of the intent JSON the extract-story-intent Activity produces and that analyze-story consumes as input.
Defines the shape of the analysis JSON produced by analyze-story and re-produced by repair-story-analysis; consumed by grade-story-analysis.
Defines the shape of the grade JSON (score, pass/fail, feedback) the Workflow inspects to decide whether to loop into repair-story-analysis or proceed/escalate.
Defines the shape of the repaired analysis JSON produced by repair-story-analysis, re-fed into grade-story-analysis on each loop iteration.

Common sentinel-file and verify-params contract (ADR-004) each skill Activity currently follows; the Workflow/Activities must decide whether to keep relying on these file-based sentinels or replace them with native Cadence Activity return values while still satisfying the 'auditable via repository state' acceptance criterion.

apis.why: Documents the `cadence` CLI commands (start, signal, describe, domain register) the story's acceptance criteria require for starting/inspecting/signaling the new Workflow.
Documents the Cadence frontend gRPC/HTTP API (StartWorkflowExecution, SignalWorkflowExecution, QueryWorkflowExecution, DescribeWorkflowExecution) referenced in the story's affected_components.api.

tests.why: Only existing Cadence Python test example in the repo; pattern to follow (per 03-python-client/testing.md) for testing the new Story Analysis Workflow and its Activities, including replay/determinism concerns.
Existing quantitative verification pattern (bash+jq schema/consistency checks) that the wrapped Activity's output should continue to satisfy so downstream skills and hooks keep working unchanged.
Existing test fixtures directory for a skill's verify.sh; indicates the repo convention of skill-local test fixtures that a new repair-story-analysis or Activity-wrapper test suite could follow.
